newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed - gas oil down on IPE.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed - gas oil down on IPE.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed with gas oil and gasoline losing some ground but fuel oil remaining steady, traders said.
Gas oil shed around $2.50 a tonne in line with September IPE futures, which was trading around $171.25.
The spot physical market was inactive with most players taking the Ascension Day holiday.

Russian 0.2 per cent sulphur heating oil was assessed at around $1.50/$2 over the cif Med high quotations cif Genoa, around unchanged. Traders continue to see a possible arbitrage to Brazil and the French Atlantic coast.

Traders said Syria had indicated that it would award cargo for a buy tender for between 50,000 and 100,000 tonnes of 0.7 percent gas oil on Tuesday. Syria has asked companies to try to improve their bids.
Gasoline lost a couple of dollars in line with easier NWE levels. Traders said U.S. futures had lost some steam which may mean the end of recent arbing from NWE.
"If that is the case then there might be cargoes to bring southwards," said one trader.
Tight supplies were not expected to improve and Italian spec cargoes were notionally pegged around high cif quotes +$3-4.
Physical high sulphur fuel was quiet but still drawing good premiums for the little offers out there with traders saying bunker spec in particular continues to be scarce.
"There's some Russian material coming out now, but it is mostly with high water content which is no good for bunkers," a trader said.
One percent was largely quiet also due to Assumption Day holiday but one trader was heard trying to bid up the quotes, traders said.
A second buyer was still heard unlikely to change from its bid of $104 cif for a low sulphur cargo but a seller was also sticking to a price $2 higher.
